text:
Mira: Heads up — saw a 2x tail latency spike on gpu-47 around 11:04 UTC, correlates with a flood of KV page faults. pprof + flamegraphs point to heavy pagewalk activity. Anyone else seeing this?

Devon: Saw it too. Pattern is repeatable under long-context workloads. When a tenant churns many distinct keys the spill queue (swapline) explodes and we start getting stalls in the batcher threads.

Oscar: Clarification: not OS swap, it's our sharded spill queue + async pagewalks. But external effect is same — IO-like latency. Repro: load with many small tenants + a few longctx requests.

Anita: I pushed a CPU flamegraph: `go tool pprof -http=localhost:6060 cpu.pb.gz` — hot stack frames around `pageWalk`, `evictScan`, and `batcher.WaitForKV`. Heap profile shows many short-lived page objects.

Kai: I think there are 3 interacting issues: 1) batcher holds KV handles across slow ops; 2) eviction scanning is quadratic when fragmentation is high; 3) tenant soft quotas don't throttle early enough.

Mira: Short-term mitigations: a) add fast circuit-breaker on tenant KV write rate; b) introduce a per-tenant "supply pool" (cap of resident pages) to limit how many pages a tenant can hold simultaneously; c) make batcher release handles when blocked > X ms.

Devon: Supply-pool sounds promising. Implementation idea: token-bucket per tenant allocated from a global supply. Borrowing allowed when global utilization < 60%, reclaimed fast when pressure rises. That lets small tenants use spare capacity but isolates noisy ones.

Oscar: If we add token-buckets, batcher integration is key. We must avoid requests blocking threads forever — either fail fast with `Retry-After` or route to smaller-model variant. Also we should expose token consumption in metrics.

Anita: Another medium-term fix: a pre-emptive demote path. Pages pinned but unused for >Y ms get demoted to LRU2 instead of full eviction; that reduces churn when reuse happens shortly after eviction. In tests that cut pagewalk ops ~30%.

Kai: Fragmentation: when tenants allocate many small context frames we end up with lots of small free slots that give the eviction scanner a bad worst-case. A compacting sweep during low traffic reduced RSS 12% in my experiment. We probably need a cheap defrag heuristic in the runtime.

Mira: I tried a synthetic noisy-neighbor run: `./bin/kvbench --tenants=240 --churn=high --longctx=8000 --pin-prob=0.25`. Repro logs attached — shows eviction storms at ~t+15m. Paste of relevant log lines:

```
# 11:04:12 gpu-47 spill-queue-size=4320 tenant=tn-193 evict-ms=124
# 11:04:15 gpu-47 pagewalks/sec=458 latency_p95_pagewalk=86ms
# 11:04:18 gpu-47 batcher-throttle=1.0 tenant=tn-193 requests_waiting=23
```

Kai: Observability wishlist: per-tenant `resident_pages`, `resident_evictions`, `avg_eviction_time`, `supply_tokens_used`, and `peak_fragmentation_ratio`. Alerts: resident_evictions rate > 50/s for 2m OR global spill-queue > threshold.

Devon: For quick triage, add a lightweight trace point when we escalate from demote->evict so we can see which tenants cause full evictions vs soft demotes. Also add a pprof flag to capture batcher stacks while spill-queue > N.

Oscar: Perf-regression note: we recently changed the eviction scan to be more aggressive to avoid longctx leaks. That change probably increased CPU on hotspots and made fragmentation worse. Revert or make it adaptive based on fragmentation ratio.

Anita: I ran a microbenchmark of demote vs evict paths. Results: demote path avg latency 6ms, full-evict 72ms under load. So prefer demote where safe.

Mira: Action items: 1) Devon will prototype per-tenant token-bucket supply pool + batcher integration (ETA 3d). 2) Anita will add demote-prefetch heuristic and compacting sweep flag for staging runs (ETA 5d). 3) Oscar will add the new metrics and alert rules to the console dashboard (ETA 2d). 4) Kai will run larger synthetic noisy-neighbor runs and capture pprof traces (ETA 2d).

sre-bot: deploy-planner: Rolling canary of `kv-runtime v2.14.3` scheduled for 2025-08-04 03:00 UTC. Will include token-bucket feature-flag.

Mira: Thanks all — if anyone has quick wins (promote demote or fail-fast fallback) please push to canary behind flags. We'll sync in eng-runtime standup tomorrow. :thumbsup:
